# MCU <-> module registers (generated)

<!-- Generated by protocol/gen from protocol/spi (the MCU <-> module SPI protocol): do not edit, regenerate. -->

The registers our code uses, from the protocol spec (`protocol/spi/src/spec.rs`). Kind: F = 2 data bytes, V = 16-bit
length + data. Access: R = the MCU reads, W = the MCU writes, N = the module notifies (0x0C names it, the MCU reads
it, F or V). Every byte on the wire is stuffed (`protocol/spi/src/framing.rs`). Evidence and the stock firmware's
handling: `docs/protocol/spi-registers.md`.

| Reg | Name | Kind | Access | Payload | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0C | PENDING | F | R | u16 | Pending: b0 = the register with queued data (0 = none). Read while PA20 is high. [RE 0x8000ca5c] |
| 0x11 | STATUS | F | RN | u16 | DM1000Status: 0x2100 ready; 0x2300 BL2 running; 0x27 asks the MCU to reboot into DFU. [RE 0x8000b684] |
| 0x25 | VERSION_IMAGE | V | R | string + NUL, <= 64 | VersionImage: the stock app's build ("I2014092908219112": the stock MCU firmware wants "9112" in stripped characters 13..16, else system error 7 [RE 0x80009340]). Ours: "zd1-os VERSION KIND" (KIND release, debug or rescue) from our OS, "zd1-boot" from our boot stub while its status says booting. Our MCU reads it at ready (and at booting): ours if it starts with "zd1-". |
| 0x28 | HCR | F | W | u16 | HCR Ctrl: 0x2100 (0x2120 from the MCU bootloader) = reboot into BL2; in BL2, 0x2220 = start an XModem download over 0x2D / 0x2C (the bootloader's relay sends it once BL2 runs) [EMU trace of the bootloader 2026-10-26]; 0x2421 factory reset. [RE] |
| 0x29 | HCR_STATUS | F | RN | u16 | HCR status: 0x2020 / 0x2120 after HCR, 0x22xx in BL2. [RE 0x8000b60c] |
| 0x2C | XM_MODULE | V | RN | bytes, <= 1029 | XModem, module -> MCU: BL2 receiving (an image through 0x2D): its control bytes 'C' / ACK / NAK / CAN, one per notification. [RE stock MCU 0x80008b40; the relay uses it, HW 2026-10-26] |
| 0x2D | XM_HOST | V | W | bytes, <= 1029 | XModem, MCU -> module: a whole XModem-1K frame (1029 bytes) per V write; a 1-byte write is a control byte (EOT). [RE stock MCU 0x80008ba0, the MCU bootloader's relay] |
| 0x32 | NET_STATUS | F | RN | 2 ASCII | NetStatus: both characters != '0' = connected (stock live: "21", also on wired). [RE 0x8000b518] |
| 0x38 | IP | V | RN | string + NUL, <= 16 | IP address string. [RE 0x8000d1b4] |
| 0x39 | NETMASK | V | RN | string + NUL, <= 16 | Netmask string (notified; not in the MCU dispatch table). [RE] |
| 0x3A | GATEWAY | V | RN | string + NUL, <= 16 | Gateway string. [RE] |
| 0x40 | VOLUME | V | RWN | volume 03 03 01 vv | Volume both ways (same handler as 0xE4): 03 03 01 vv; also the 03 01 handshake. [RE 0x8000b32c] |
| 0x45 | CONFIG | V | RWN | config [op][n][name][value] | Configuration channel: reads reply by notification on 0x45. Ours: names `zd1/KEY` are our settings, `zd1/@N` our records by number (the host link's `Record`; docs/module/settings.md). [RE 0x8000b458] |
| 0x47 | DRC_XML | V | RN | DRC XML | DRC XML: the play icon pl / pa / em; pl makes the MCU switch to Wi-Fi. [RE] |
| 0x48 | DRC | F | W | DRC code | DRC command (b0, [`Drc`]); some acknowledged on 0xE3. [RE] |
| 0x58 | DEVICE_NAME | V | RN | text, <= 64 | DeviceName (no NUL from the stock module). [RE] |
| 0x5A | ACTIVE_PROFILE | F | RWN | 2 ASCII | ActiveWirelessProfile: b0 = '0' + n. [RE] |
| 0xC0 | INTENT | F | RN | u16 | Ours: a person picked one of our OS's receivers (the speaker chosen on a phone for AirPlay: the sender's first SETUP; in a Spotify app): b0 = the [`player`] receiver, b1 counts up (each pick is a new value). zd1-linkd has made it the receiver in front (the others pause); the MCU switches to the module at once, as a choice made by hand, acknowledges it on the LED and starts the amp. |
| 0xC1 | DEBUG | F | W | u16 | Ours: the module OS's debug services: b0 = 0 the image's default (zd1.debug), 1 on, 2 off (host::Debug). The MCU writes it at every ready of our OS once set, and when it changes. |
| 0xC2 | SELECT | F | W | u16 | Ours: b0 = a [`player`] receiver to bring to the front, as a person chose it on the speaker (the ON/OFF key, the host link's Select): zd1-linkd tells the others to pause their senders and that one to resume. |
| 0xC3 | MCU_VERSION | V | W | string + NUL, <= 48 | Ours: the MCU firmware's version, written at every ready of our OS (the module keeps it in /run/zd1/mcu-version). |
| 0xC4 | BOOT | F | RW | u16 | Ours: what the boot stub starts (module/boot linuxboot, identified as "zd1-boot" on 0x25 while its status says booting): b0 = a [`boot`] value, b1 = the good slot. The MCU writes it once per boot of the stub (it reads 0 until then); without an answer the stub starts the rescue. The MCU writes it to our OS at ready too: what it runs and the good slot (a trial confirmed by that ready). |
| 0xC5 | UPDATE | V | W | bytes, <= 128 | Ours: start the updater (zd1-update, docs/module/updater.md): size u32, baud u32 (little-endian), sha256 [32], the stamp (ASCII, the rest). The system image follows on the module console's UART at that baud, in frames the module answers (docs/module/updater.md); its lines (0x02 text \n) say ready, ok or error. |
| 0xC6 | PLAYER | V | RN | bytes, <= 3 | Ours: our OS's receivers: [0] the one in front (a [`player`] receiver: the one playing, else the last one paused or chosen), [1] its [`player`] state, [2] the receivers with a sender connected (bit = the receiver's value: an AirPlay sender, a Spotify Connect session, a snapserver). Notified by zd1-linkd when any of it changes (its arbitration: the newest `playing` source owns the speaker) and once our MCU firmware has written 0xC3; never before (a stock host can't read it and its queue would stay stuck on it). The MCU's source list, LED and auto-switch use it: a receiver's playing switches the source and wakes the speaker (zd1-linkd sends no 0x47). |
| 0xD2 | SPEAKER | V | W | bytes, <= 4 | Ours, native ([`LINK_PROTO`]): the speaker, as our OS should see it: [0] [`native::PROTO`], [1] the module's volume, a step (0..71: the speaker's, or one the module asked for that waits for it to be the input), [2] the highest step the module may ask for (the cap; a sender's whole range maps onto 0..cap), [3] [`native`] flags (the module is the input). Written after 0xC3 at every hello and whenever any of it changes, the volume also after every 0xD4 (what was applied: the cap, the knob). |
| 0xD3 | KEY | F | W | u16 | Ours, native: a key a person pressed for the module (the speaker's keys, the remote, the host link's Key, a USB host's media keys while the module is the input): b0 a [`native`] key, b1 counts up. Only presses: entering and leaving the module's input are 0xD2's flag, a receiver chosen on the speaker is 0xC2. |
| 0xD4 | VOLUME_SET | F | RN | u16 | Ours, native: our OS asks for a volume: b0 a step 0..the cap (0xD2 [2]). Applied at once while the module is the input, else when it becomes it (a later knob change wins); the result comes back on 0xD2. |
| 0xD5 | LINK_PROTO | F | R | u16 | Ours: the protocol our OS speaks, b1 ([`native::PROTO`]). The MCU reads it at every hello; another value than its own makes the module no source (the base layer still works). |
| 0xD6 | STATE | V | N | bytes, <= 1024 | Ours, native: the State record (the host link's `State` message: the module's settings and status, encoded by the module with the host link's codec). Notified after every hello and when something in it changes (at most once a second); the MCU keeps the last copy and serves it to the host (`ModRecord State`) without asking the module. |
| 0xE2 | SHUTDOWN | F | WN | u16 | Shutdown: the MCU writes 00 00, the module answers 01 00, then power off. [RE] |
| 0xE3 | DRC_ACK | F | RN | u16 | AirTunesPlaybackStatus: the DRC acks (b0). [RE] |
| 0xE4 | VOLUME_HOST | V | RN | volume 03 03 01 vv | VolumeHostChange: as 0x40. [RE] |

## DRC codes (0x48, b0)

| Code | Name | Ack (0xE3 b0) | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x9D | JbcStart | - | JBConnect: start the setup network (after Networking/JBCONNECT/JBCSSID). |
| 0x9E | WirelessApply | - | Re-apply the wireless settings (sent when NetIF/mode was set to wireless). |
| 0x9F | JbcStop | - | JBConnect: stop the setup network. |
| 0xB0 | Next | - | Next track (key/IR on the Wi-Fi source). |
| 0xB1 | Prev | - | Previous track. |
| 0xB3 | PlayPause | - | Play/pause toggle (IR). |
| 0xDE | Pause | 1 | Pause: leaving the Wi-Fi source (other source, standby, iPod docked). |
| 0xDF | Play | 0 | Play/resume: entering the Wi-Fi source, and the startup resume. |
| 0xE1 | Release | 4 | Release the audio path: leaving Wi-Fi for a local source or standby. |
| 0xE2 | Enable | 5 | (Re)enable the audio path: entering the Wi-Fi source, and at boot. |
